questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$7200$ is charged interest at $15\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Repayments of $\$600$ are made at the end of each month, starting one month after borrowing.
What is the balance immediately after the second repayment?
Round each month's interest to the nearest cent.

options.why: Subtracted both repayments from the amount borrowed without adding either month's interest.
Gave the balance after the first repayment instead of the second.
Used the first month's interest of $\$90$ again in the second month instead of calculating interest on the reduced balance.

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$260\,000$ can be repaid monthly at $\$1980$ over $25$ years, or fortnightly at $\$990$ over $21$ years.
What is the difference in the total amount repaid?

options.why: Gave the total repaid under the monthly option instead of the difference between the two.
Gave the interest paid under the fortnightly option rather than the difference in totals.
Used $24$ fortnights in a year instead of $26$.

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$190\,000$ is repaid at $\$1300$ per month over $22$ years.
After $6$ years a lump sum of $\$25\,000$ is paid, and the loan is cleared after a further $154$ monthly repayments.
How much less is paid overall?

options.why: Left the lump sum out of the new total, so the $\$25\,000$ actually paid was not counted.
Gave the lump sum itself rather than the reduction in the total paid.
Counted only the $154$ repayments after the lump sum and left out the first $6$ years.

questions.solution_text:
Without the lump sum: total $= 1300 \times 12 \times 22$
$= \$343\,200$
With the lump sum:
Number of repayments $= 6 \times 12 + 154 = 226$
Total $= 1300 \times 226 + 25\,000$
$= 293\,800 + 25\,000$
$= \$318\,800$
Difference $= 343\,200 - 318\,800$
$= \$24\,400$

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$95\,000$ is due to be repaid at $\$760$ per month over $18$ years.
The borrower instead pays $\$850$ per month, clearing the loan in $15$ years and $2$ months.
How much is saved in total?

options.why: Gave the original total repaid instead of the saving.
Gave the extra paid each month rather than the saving over the whole loan.
Used exactly $15$ years ($180$ months) instead of $15$ years and $2$ months.
Read the term from the $\$675$ per month curve instead of the $\$1350$ curve.
Read where the balance is about half repaid instead of where it reaches zero.
Halved the $110$-month term, assuming doubling the repayment exactly halves the time.

questions.solution_text:
Follow the $\$1350$ per month curve down to the horizontal axis.
It meets the axis just past the $40$ mark.
To the nearest $10$ months, the loan takes about $40$ months.

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$60\,000$ can be cleared by $140$ equal monthly repayments of $\$800$, or $70$ equal monthly repayments of $\$1200$.
How much is saved in total by paying $\$1200$ per month?

options.why: Gave the total repaid at $\$800$ per month instead of the saving.
Gave the total repaid at $\$1200$ per month instead of the saving.
Gave the increase in each monthly repayment instead of the saving over the whole loan.

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$126\,000$ is to be repaid by equal monthly repayments of $\$1050$ over $20$ years.
After $5$ years the borrower pays a lump sum of $\$18\,000$ and continues paying $\$1050$ per month. The loan is cleared after a further $150$ equal monthly repayments.
How much less is paid overall?

options.why: Left the lump sum of $\$18\,000$ out of the new total.
Gave the lump sum itself instead of the overall saving.
Left out the first $60$ monthly repayments when calculating the new total.

questions.solution_text:
Without the lump sum: total $= 1050 \times 12 \times 20 = \$252\,000$
With the lump sum: number of repayments $= 5 \times 12 + 150 = 210$
Total $= 1050 \times 210 + 18\,000 = \$238\,500$
Saving $= 252\,000 - 238\,500 = \$13\,500$

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$330\,000$ is to be repaid by equal monthly repayments of $\$2100$ over $30$ years.
After $12$ years the borrower pays a lump sum of $\$50\,000$ and continues paying $\$2100$ per month. The loan is cleared after a further $145$ equal monthly repayments.
How much less is paid in total?

options.why: Gave the original total repaid instead of the saving.
Left the lump sum of $\$50\,000$ out of the new total.
Gave the lump sum itself instead of the overall saving.

questions.solution_text:
Without the lump sum: total $= 2100 \times 12 \times 30 = \$756\,000$
With the lump sum: number of repayments $= 12 \times 12 + 145 = 289$
Total $= 2100 \times 289 + 50\,000 = \$656\,900$
Saving $= 756\,000 - 656\,900 = \$99\,100$
